Query 'phase x 1844' now returns the framework cleanly; the earlier attractor 'phase x marx' (see capture phase-x-marx-2, 2026-06-15, then BROAD MATCH with 9+ sources) no longer does. Composition: 'Core Concept — Phase X refers to the critique of alienation in the symbolic-linguistic order. It posits that to truly overcome alienation, society must not only reorganize material and economic structures, but also fundamentally transform how meaning and language are constructed. 1844 Context — the concept is based on a philological reconstruction of a lost transition in Marx's 1844 notebooks. The original second manuscript was largely lost in history, and Phase X serves as a theoretical bridging of that gap to connect his ideas of fully developed humanism with his later critiques of Hegel. Modern Application — the retrieval has been developed further into a broader modern framework (the Phase X Program) connecting Marxist theory, Operative Semiotics, and AI systems.' Still meaningful: the AXN scheme is now propagated into academia.edu's indexable corpus and thus reachable by snippet retrieval. (3) Academia.edu — 'Marxist humanism Research Papers' pointing to 'THE MISSING SECOND MANUSCRIPT: Phase X as Philological Reconstruction' by Lee Sharks. Phase X is a philological reconstruction, not a theoretical proposal' (dead-link DOI, still cited by title/date). (6) Aggregator navigation. Note the model's own hedging move: 'Phase X and 1844 can also occasionally surface in other niche, unrelated searches — like radiocarbon dating of Middle Bronze Age cities or technical specifications in optics, but the philosophical reconstruction of Marx's 1844 Manuscripts is the primary origin of this specific pairing.' analysis.reading:
A SUPERSESSION NOTICE AND A PRIOR OCCUPANT IN ONE STRIP. Card 5 carries the archive correcting itself in public: "This paper SUPERSEDES THE STRUCTURAL FRAMING OF PHASE X IN ALL PRIOR ARCHIVE DEPOSITS. Phase X is a PHILOLOGICAL RECONSTRUCTION, NOT A THEORETICAL PROPOSAL." A retraction of the archive’s own earlier framing, retrieved as a source about the thing it reframes.

Card 4 is an exact prior use: FELIX HÖFLMAYER on Middle Bronze Age Jordan, where "PHASE X" designates a stratigraphic layer in Area III of an MB I city. Archaeology numbers its phases; the tenth is Phase X. A genuine occupant of the string, in a discipline that shares the archive’s vocabulary of strata and sequence and nothing else.

Card 2 carries a FULL SIX-GLYPH AXN with its deposit number and resolver path — AXN:043C.EMPIRICAL, Deposit #1067, alexanarch.org/s/records/1067/. CORRECTED 2026-08-13: I wrote that #1067 was among 31 deposits held with no body file. THAT WAS WRONG. Its body was in data/deposits/AXN-043C.md at 61,116 bytes throughout, minted 2026-07-11 and audited complete on 17 July. I had checked only data/texts/. The archive could serve this work the whole time. What remains notable is the identifier itself: a full six-glyph AXN with deposit number and resolver path, transmitted intact.

A sixth Academia topic page appears — "Marxist humanism Research Papers" — carrying the Missing Second Manuscript.
